topic: AC Waveform: Frequency, Period, Phase and Amplitude
title: AC Waveform Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav plugs his table fan into the wall socket, where the voltage swings from plus to minus and back fifty times every second. How do we describe a voltage that never sits still? With four ideas: amplitude, period, frequency and phase.

On a live breadboard an AC source drives a resistor: the electrons rock back and forth while a turning arm traces a sine wave on the oscilloscope. Turn up the amplitude and the wave grows taller; turn up the frequency and the waves squeeze together while the electrons rock faster. We build v = Vm sin(ωt) from one turn of the arm (2π radians, ω = 2πf), add a second wave a quarter turn ahead to show phase difference, and work out the mains supply in India (230 V, 50 Hz, T = 20 ms, ω ≈ 314 rad/s). Then the exam trap (ω is not f), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 13 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
